metadata.rules_text:
- Model consistently overestimates prices in early forecast windows, especially after sharp spikes; apply downward bias correction for first 5–7 days post-spike.
- Overshoots in mid-to-late forecast horizon (days 10–25) often occur when sentiment is neutral or slightly negative; reduce forecast peak values by 5–10% if sentiment remains flat.
- Mean reversion bias is evident: model tends to overreact to recent highs/lows; apply smoothing filter or decay factor to recent price movements (e.g., 30% weight on last 3 days).
- When sentiment history is uniformly zero (no market sentiment signal), model should not assume strong directional bias; use historical volatility or range-bound models instead.
- Forecast horizon 30d shows persistent underestimation of true price volatility; increase forecast variance or add stochastic adjustment for high-uncertainty periods.
- If true outcome shows sharp reversal after a forecast peak, model should reduce forecast slope for next 3–5 days; apply “reversal buffer” rule: if forecast > true outcome by >10%, reduce next forecast by 15–20%.
- No sentiment signal → no directional bias; forecast should be centered around recent 7-day moving average unless event-driven context overrides.
